**Group:** Ciliates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A loricate ciliate: the cell secretes and sits inside a lorica — a cup-, vase-, trumpet-, or tube-shaped shell that may be transparent (hyaline) or built up from agglomerated particles. The ciliate body attaches at the closed end, and a crown of oral ciliary membranelles projects from the wide open mouth when feeding. Lorica shape and ornamentation are the main field characters. Key features: distinct external lorica, oral membranelle crown, a single cell inside the shell.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **tiarina** | Tintinnids sit inside an external lorica (shell); Tiarina and other naked ciliates have no lorica. |
| **phaeocystis** | Phaeocystis is a gelatinous colony of many cells; a tintinnid is one ciliate cell inside a firm lorica. |
